name: Low orbit, low cost
summary: A 3U CubeSat at 500 km, launched as a rideshare, with one ground station near the North Pole.
trade_off: The cheapest design here that meets every requirement. At 500 km the thin air slowly drags the spacecraft down, so it carries a small thruster to keep its height.
source: Combination of parts from this folder, chosen by searching every design the catalogue allows. See docs/model-assumptions.md, section 7.

name: More pictures, two stations
summary: The same spacecraft, taking pictures for longer each day and sending them down through two ground stations.
trade_off: Returns much more data than the requirement asks for, which gives margin if a station is lost. The second station costs about US$2 million more over the mission.
source: Combination of parts from this folder, chosen by searching every design the catalogue allows. See docs/model-assumptions.md, section 7.

name: High orbit, own rocket
summary: A light 3U CubeSat with no thruster, flown to Landsat's 705 km orbit on its own small rocket.
trade_off: At 705 km the air is so thin that the orbit lasts the whole mission without a thruster, so this is the lightest design. No rideshare here goes to that orbit, so the rocket takes most of the budget.
source: Combination of parts from this folder, chosen by searching every design the catalogue allows. See docs/model-assumptions.md, section 7.

name: Room to grow, 6U frame
summary: The low-orbit design built on a frame twice the size, with bigger fold-out solar wings.
trade_off: There is space and power left over for more parts. It weighs more and costs a little more for the same science, so it scores slightly lower.
